02 April 2012 

Precious metal prices were generally weak in the 
final days of March with only gold managing to hold 
onto any gains in Dollar terms despite a relatively 
firm Euro. The initial downwards impetus came from 
concerns over European debt and slowing Chinese 
growth, sending all of the metals to lows on the 
22nd of March. A strengthening Euro provided sup-
port and each metal moved higher, with further im-
petus provided by comments from Ben Bernanke 
on the 26th that US accommodative policies were 
likely to be maintained. The strength was tempo-
rary, though, with the complex sagging lower since 
that point. In the first weeks of 2012, the more in-
dustrial metals had outperformed gold but now the 
tables were turned: gold regained its recent pre-
mium over platinum to suggest that risk appetite 
had decreased noticeably. 
 

After the previous week’s long liquidation of futures 
positions, investors treated the precious metals 
complex with a little more discrimination leading up 
to the 27th of March. Gold positioning rebounded, 
climbing by two million ounces. However, futures 
investors continued to be bearish on the more in-
dustrial precious metals, with short positioning ris-
ing and long positions being closed for palladium, 
platinum and silver. 
 

ETF flows in the last week of March were more 
positive than in the preceding week. Gold saw a 
little net selling but nothing like the 500,000 ounces 
sold a week earlier. Platinum and silver saw buyers 
tempted in by lower prices and recorded net inflows 
of metal into their funds. Palladium too saw buying 
interest but this was outweighed by heavy selling 
from one of the smaller funds.

Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 
 
02 April 2012 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Gold was the only one of the four major precious 
metals to see its price rise in the final ten days of 
March, as it climbed from $1,665 to $1,675. Un-
surprisingly, fears over European debt and a Chi-
nese economic slowdown hurt the more industrial 
metals more than gold. Nevertheless, gold’s price 
performance was not exciting, suggesting that 
investor attention has moved elsewhere for the 
moment. What was perhaps more interesting as a 
gauge of market sentiment was that gold moved 
back over platinum, suggesting that a global eco-
nomic recovery is by no means a certainty. Dur-
ing the week, gold did fall as low as $1,630 on the 
22nd before rallying to $1,695 on the 27th follow-
ing assistance from a weak Dollar and comments 
from 
Ben 
Bernanke 
suggesting 
that 
“accommodative policies” might be maintained. 
The boost was short-lived though, with selling re-
emerging to leave gold at $1,670 at the end of the 
month. 
 

Net long speculative COMEX positions bounced 
by 2.2 million ounces in the week to the 27th of 
March, with short-covering of some futures posi-
tions accompanied by addition to outright long 
positions. The response of futures investors to 
the decline in price has been rather lukewarm, 
with positions now some 7.7 million ounces lower 
than at the end of February. There are two possi-
ble interpretations of this move: a los of investor 
confidence or space for a move higher at some 
point. We feel that a sense of short term bearish-
ness has entered the market and that the reality 
lies between these two positions. 
 

After the previous week’s net ETF selling of al-
most half a million ounces of gold, the final week 
of March was more neutral with only 16,000 
ounces sold. Worryingly, however, the majority of 
funds which we monitor recorded net outflows of 
metal (roughly balanced by buying in GLD/
SPDR). As we wrote last week, this suggests that 
investors are beginning to become a little less 
convinced of the bullish case for gold. Total posi-
tions now stand at 70.4 million ounces.

Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 
 
02 April 2012 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Silver ETF Investment, Jan 08 — Mar 12 

The last ten days of March were relatively quiet 
for the silver price which traded only in a $2 
range. The initial move during this period was 
lower as the after-effects of the 29th of February 
sell-off continued to erode investor confidence. 
Silver continued to drift lower from nearly $37 
then to a low of $31.15 on the 22nd as gold fell. 
At this point, a stronger Euro provided some as-
sistance, helping silver back to a high of $33.16 
on the 27th before confidence waned once again, 
with silver falling back to end the month close to 
$32.50 per ounce. Currently, silver is largely fol-
lowing the gold price and showing little independ-
ence but it may be challenging for silver to main-
tain this performance if futures investors continue 
to liquidate their positions. 
 

In the silver market, net long speculative positions 
decreased for a fourth successive week, dropping 
by 15.7 million ounces to 169.1 million ounces on 
COMEX. Since the end of February, positioning 
has fallen from 257 million ounces. Little addi-
tional short interest has been seen but long posi-
tions have been pared back to more reasonable 
levels. Although the silver price fell back sharply 
at the end of February and the start of March, it 
has been surprisingly robust, finding support 
above $32 despite this reduction in futures inter-
est. 
 

After two weeks of net selling, silver ETF posi-
tions increased by 910,000 ounces to 460 million 
ounces in the final week of March. The buying 
interest was fairly widespread with a number of 
funds recording fresh buying interest. Overall, 
though, there is still no clear indication of momen-
tum amongst ETF silver investors.

Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 
 
02 April 2012 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Platinum trading was mixed in the final days of 
March. Initially, the price fell from the 21st over 
concerns of slow or slowing Chinese economic 
growth. Interestingly, platinum underperformed 
gold even as gold struggled with platinum moving 
back into an unaccustomed discount to the yellow 
metal. Overall, platinum declined from $1,680 on 
the 19th to a brief low of $1,605 on the 22nd be-
fore the selling dissipated. A firmer Euro helped 
provide a little support for platinum and the other 
metals and investors did the rest of the work in 
taking the price back up to $1,665 on the 27th. 
Bearish sentiment slowly descended on the mar-
ket though and, with gold weak, platinum softened 
towards support at the $1,640 level. 
 

Net long speculative NYMEX positions in platinum 
dropped for the fourth successive week. Investors 
shed a further 112,000 ounces as positions slid 
from 1.78  million ounces at the end of February to 
1.61 million ounces at the end of March, as TO-
COM positions climbed by 36,000 ounces. The 
selling has been quite orderly and mainly driven 
by long liquidation. However, a recent rise in the 
number of open short contracts could indicate fur-
ther price weakness ahead. 
 

Platinum bulls breathed a sigh of relief in the final 
week of March as ETF investors returned tenta-
tively to buying mode after three successive 
weeks of selling had been seen. While there was 
a small amount of selling of metal from one of the 
smaller funds, this was outweighed by some gen-
tle buying in the European ETFS fund. Total hold-
ings currently stand at 1.49 million ounces, thirty 
thousand ounces below their March peak.

Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 
 
02 April 2012 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Palladium Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Mar 12 
Palladium ETF Investment, Apr 07 — Mar 12 

In the second half of March, palladium emphati-
cally fell below support at $700 per ounce to touch 
a low of $641. Of itself, this price decline was not 
too surprising. Of greater concern was the fact that 
no real attempt was made to recapture this level. 
On the 22nd, disappointing Chinese PMI data set a 
bearish tone and all of the precious metals were 
sold. Having been flirting with the $700 level a day 
earlier, palladium dropped to a low of $650 on the 
22nd before finding support. The Euro strength-
ened slowly but steadily against the US Dollar, pro-
viding some respite and helping palladium recover 
a little of its lost ground in reaching $670 on the 
27th. Gentle selling pressure re-emerged to send 
palladium to close to $640 on the 29th although it 
has since recovered to $659. 
 

Having slipped below $700, palladium lost some of 
its appeal to investors who cut their net long expo-
sure to palladium in response. In the week to the 
27th of March, NYMEX positioning fell by 291,000 
ounces, their largest weekly fall since September 
2011.  Net positioning remains moderate by histori-
cal standards at 911,000 ounces following a spell 
of long liquidation and additions to short position-
ing. Non-commercial short positions climbed to 
3,200 contracts but this remains much lower than 
in Q4 last year. 
 

While platinum saw net ETF buying in the final 
week of March, palladium saw a mixture of buying 
and selling even as the price failed to rebound fol-
lowing its fall from $700. US investors proved to be 
positive, buying half a tonne of metal, treating the 
price fall as a buying opportunity. However, there 
was a large sale of metal from one of the smaller 
funds we monitor, which drove net positions down 
by 8,000 ounces in the week to 1.97 million 
ounces. We believe that this is likely to have been 
the action of a single investor and feel that the 
dominant view is that current prices provide a buy-
ing opportunity.
